messages:
ashley: Dropping a new prototype: a combined scrub + precise selector for the latency heatmap. Toggle called 'Scrub' (fast swipes) vs 'Precision' (manual from/to inputs + presets). Video + notes: https://uploads/redwood/protos/scrub-precision.mp4

sam: watched it. Feels smooth. Question: during a fast scrub the p95 band redraws a lot  can we debounce redraws to keep GPU/cpu usage down? maybe update buckets every 200ms instead of on every frame.

marta: agree on debounce. UX thought: while scrubbing show a lightweight overlay with a condensed sparkline and a tiny pill with the exact timestamps. When settled, commit the full heatmap. That avoids the flicker.

ben: design detail: the pill should show sampling rate state too (e.g., "1/20 sampled"). If users change sampling, they expect metrics to refresh differently. Also prefer a subtle dashed outline around the overlay so it reads as a preview, not the real data.

ashley: noted. I'm experimenting with moving sampling controls into the time selector itself rather than a top toolbar toggle. The idea: sampling is contextual per-range and defaults to global. There would be a small "sample: 1/10" chip in the selector with a chevron for options: range/global/full.

jin: contextual is handy but we must avoid surprising people. Proposal: when a user changes range sampling, show a transient toast: "Sampling changed for this range. Set as default? [Yes] [No]" so people can promote to global. Also log telemetry with origin=range-picker.

a11y-bot: accessibility: ensure the chip has 4.5:1 text contrast, and the dashed outline has sufficient non-text contrast (3:1). Also the preview sparkline must have an accessible label and the chip needs role=button with aria-expanded for the flyout. Keyboard users should be able to toggle scrub/precision via Space/Enter when focused.

sam: keyboard we should spec: focus on time control -> Tab cycles to mode toggle -> Enter opens presets -> Arrow keys move start/end by preset step -> Shift+Arrow expand/shrink range. I'll write the keyboard sequence and edge cases.

marta: copy suggestions for the flyout header: short: "Sampling for this range" and a helper line: "Lower resolution speeds up queries; sampled p95 may miss brief spikes." For the p95 card we should surface an inline hint when sampled: "p95 (sampled)" with a tooltip explaining fidelity implications.

ben: mobile note: on small widths the chip should collapse to an icon-only control. Tapping icon opens full selector. Also confirm gesture inertia on Android/iOS feels natural and doesn't trigger accidental presets.

ashley: action list: Ben -> icon-only mobile mock + overlay dashed states (today), Sam -> keyboard spec + debounce numbers (tomorrow), Marta -> final microcopy + tooltip text (tomorrow), Jin -> telemetry naming + default promotion flow (next sprint), a11y-bot -> run checks once mocks land. I'll update the prototype to include the sampling chip in the time selector and wire the toast.

marta: one last UX safety: when sampling is enabled and the p95 drops significantly compared to full, show a small banner: "Sampled data may underreport spikes. View full range to confirm." linked to a toggle to load full fidelity.

sam: +1. Also add an experiment flag: `range_sampling_ui` so we can slowly roll this to users.

ashley: perfect. I'll open the experiment RFC and attach the prototype. Thanks everyone!
